questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of unit testing?

options.text: To test the entire system's functionality.
To test individual components of the software.
To check how components interact with each other.
To find and fix user interface bugs.

questions.explanation: Unit testing focuses on testing individual components to ensure they work as intended. This helps catch errors early in the development process.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect because unit testing does not evaluate the entire system.
distractorRationale.b: Option c describes integration testing, not unit testing.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is not specific to unit testing, as it pertains to user interface issues.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a fault in software?

options.text: An incorrect output from the software.
A defect in the software code.
A mistake made by the developer.
A failure of the software to meet user needs.

questions.explanation: A fault is specifically a defect in the code that can lead to failures when the software is executed. Understanding this distinction is crucial in software engineering.

distractorRationale.a: Option a describes a failure, not a fault.
distractorRationale.b: Option c refers to an error, which is a different concept.
distractorRationale.c: Option d relates to the software's performance but does not define a fault.

questions.stem: Debugging is only necessary after the software has been fully developed.
questions.explanation: Debugging should be an ongoing process throughout software development, not just after completion. Identifying issues early can save time and resources.

questions.stem: What does code coverage measure in unit testing?

options.text: The number of bugs in the code.
The percentage of code executed during tests.

questions.explanation: Code coverage measures how much of the code is executed during tests, indicating which parts of the codebase are tested and which are not.

distractorRationale.b: Option c refers to performance metrics, not coverage.
